newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ansett to start China flights, Qantas expands.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ansett to start China flights, Qantas expands.

text.p: Australia's International Air Services Commission said it would allow Ansett Australia to begin flights to China and permit Qantas Airways Ltd to expand services on that route.
Commission chairman Jim Bain said in a statement the decision would result in a further eight services being introduced between Sydney/Melbourne and Beijing over the next two years.
The services to Kuala Lumpur would operate via Jakarta and bring to six the number of services operated on the route.
This capacity would enable Ansett to expand to a daily flights by mid-1997.
The Commission also allocated new capacity to Qantas on the Australia - South Africa route.

Qantas, 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc, could now provide two additional flights per week in each direction, enabling Qantas to introduce scheduled services linking Melbourne to Johannesburg for the first time.
